chapter.title: Deriving PageRank
chapter.subtitle: From a random walk to a score
chapter.sub: Chapter four: deriving PageRank. We will work it out by hand, one small step at a time.
chapter.tts: Chapter four. Deriving PageRank. We will work it out by hand, one small step at a time.

lines.sub: I will build PageRank from scratch, in a very small world.
lines.tts: I will build PageRank from scratch, in a very small world.

lines.sub: There are four nodes and four allowance edges, drawn as arrows.
lines.tts: There are four nodes and four allowance edges, drawn as arrows.

lines.sub: Node A is a token owner, that is, a person's wallet address.
lines.tts: Node A is a token owner, that is, a person's wallet address.

lines.sub: This kind of address is called an EOA.
lines.tts: This kind of address is called an E O A.

lines.sub: B and C are vault contracts that node A has approved.
lines.tts: B and C are vault contracts that node A has approved.

lines.sub: D is a lending pool contract, and both vaults approve it in turn.
lines.tts: D is a lending pool contract, and both vaults approve it in turn.

lines.sub: This is the same as the worked example in Chapter 2 of the thesis.
lines.tts: This is the same as the worked example in Chapter two of the thesis.

lines.sub: The number on each arrow is its weight.
lines.tts: The number on each arrow is its weight.

lines.sub: The bigger the weight, the thicker the arrow.
lines.tts: The bigger the weight, the thicker the arrow.

lines.sub: I write the weight of the arrow from u to v as w(u, v).
lines.tts: I write the weight of the arrow from u to v as w of u and v.

lines.sub: So A to B is 2, and A to C is 1.
lines.tts: So from A to B it is two, and from A to C it is one.

lines.sub: B to D is 3, and C to D is 1.
lines.tts: B to D is three, and C to D is one.

lines.sub: The sum of all the weights leaving a node u, I call o(u).
lines.tts: The sum of all the weights leaving a node u, I call o of u.

lines.sub: The Σ in the formula is the symbol for “add them all up”.
lines.tts: The sigma in the formula is the symbol for add them all up.

lines.sub: The small v underneath means we add while v runs over the nodes.
lines.tts: The small v underneath means we add while v runs over the nodes.

lines.sub: So o(A) is 2 + 1, which is 3.
lines.tts: So o of A is two plus one, which is three.

lines.sub: o(B) is 3, and o(C) is 1.
lines.tts: o of B is three, and o of C is one.

lines.sub: D has no outgoing arrow at all, so o(D) is 0.
lines.tts: D has no outgoing arrow at all, so o of D is zero.

lines.sub: Keep an eye on this 0. It is about to cause trouble.
lines.tts: Keep an eye on this zero. It is about to cause trouble.

lines.sub: Now I let one person loose in this world.
lines.tts: Now I let one person loose in this world.

lines.sub: They wander around without any plan. Let's call them the random walker.
lines.tts: They wander around without any plan. Let's call them the random walker.

card.title: Random walker
card.body: Someone who moves along arrows at random, heavier arrows more often

lines.sub: There is one rule. From the node where they stand, they pick one outgoing arrow.
lines.tts: There is one rule. From the node where they stand, they pick one outgoing arrow.

lines.sub: And they pick heavier arrows more often.
lines.tts: And they pick heavier arrows more often.

lines.sub: I spin the spinner next to node A.
lines.tts: I spin the spinner next to node A.

lines.sub: Of its three slices, two are B and one is C.
lines.tts: Of its three slices, two are B and one is C.

lines.sub: The weights 2 and 1 have simply become the numbers of slices.
lines.tts: The weights two and one have simply become the numbers of slices.

lines.sub: This time it lands on B, so the walker crosses to B. See the white dot there.
lines.tts: This time it lands on B, so the walker crosses to B. See the white dot there.

lines.sub: Of A's total weight, 3, the part pointing toward B is 2.
lines.tts: Of the total weight of node A, three, the part pointing toward B is two.

lines.sub: So two times out of three, the walker goes to B.
lines.tts: So two times out of three, the walker goes to B.

lines.sub: I write this probability as P. Here, P_A,B, the chance of going from A to B, is 2/3.
lines.tts: I write this probability as P. Here, P of A to B, the chance of going from A to B, is two thirds.

lines.sub: In general, we divide the weight of an arrow by the sum of the weights leaving its node.
lines.tts: In general, we divide the weight of an arrow by the sum of the weights leaving its node.

lines.sub: In the same way, A to C is 1/3.
lines.tts: In the same way, from A to C it is one third.

lines.sub: From B and from C there is only one way out, so the walker always goes to D.
lines.tts: From B and from C there is only one way out, so the walker always goes to D.

lines.sub: The probabilities leaving a node always add up to 1. For A, 2/3 + 1/3 = 1.
lines.tts: The probabilities leaving a node always add up to one. For node A, two thirds plus one third is one.

lines.sub: D is the only exception, because there is nothing to add.
lines.tts: D is the only exception, because there is nothing to add.

lines.sub: Next, the walker stands at B. Spinning B's spinner can only give D.
lines.tts: Next, the walker stands at B. Spinning B's spinner can only give D.

lines.sub: So the walker moves on to D.
lines.tts: So the walker moves on to D.

lines.sub: But D has no arrow to leave by, so the walk gets stuck.
lines.tts: But D has no arrow to leave by, so the walk gets stuck.

lines.sub: Also, B to D is the only way out of B.
lines.tts: Also, B to D is the only way out of B.

lines.sub: So even with weight 3, the probability is 1.
lines.tts: So even with weight three, the probability is one.

lines.sub: Weights only matter where the path forks, as it does at node A.
lines.tts: Weights only matter where the path forks, as it does at node A.

lines.sub: Set that dead end aside for a moment, and imagine this person walks for a very long time.
lines.tts: Set that dead end aside for a moment, and imagine this person walks for a very long time.

lines.sub: Then the fraction of time spent at each node settles down.
lines.tts: Then the fraction of time spent at each node settles down.

lines.sub: PageRank uses exactly this fraction as the node's score, which we call r.
lines.tts: PageRank uses exactly this fraction as the node's score, which we call r.

lines.sub: Here is a second picture. Instead of one person, think of 1 liter of water.
lines.tts: Here is a second picture. Instead of one person, think of one liter of water.

lines.sub: You can also picture the person split into very many droplets.
lines.tts: You can also picture the person split into very many droplets.

lines.sub: At first, I put a quarter, 0.25, into each of the four cups under the nodes.
lines.tts: At first, I put a quarter, zero point two five, into each of the four cups under the nodes.

lines.sub: I write the water in the cup of node v as r_v.
lines.tts: I write the water in the cup of node v as r of v.

lines.sub: This is the node's share, that is, its score.
lines.tts: This is the node's share, that is, its score.

lines.sub: Now I pour once.
lines.tts: Now I pour once.

lines.sub: The water in each cup is split along the outgoing arrows, in proportion to their probabilities.
lines.tts: The water in each cup is split along the outgoing arrows, in proportion to their probabilities.

lines.sub: A's water goes to B and C at 2 to 1.
lines.tts: The water of node A goes to B and C at two to one.

lines.sub: Notice that A's cup is now empty.
lines.tts: Notice that the cup of node A is now empty.

lines.sub: All of B's and C's water goes to D.
lines.tts: All of B's and C's water goes to D.

lines.sub: But D's water has no way out, so it spills away.
lines.tts: But D's water has no way out, so it spills away.

lines.sub: We come back to this leak two slides from now.
lines.tts: We come back to this leak two slides from now.

lines.sub: If we keep pouring like this, there comes a point where the amount in each cup no longer changes.
lines.tts: If we keep pouring like this, there comes a point where the amount in each cup no longer changes.

lines.sub: We call this balance.
lines.tts: We call this balance.

card.title: Balance
card.body: Each cup's level holds, because as much flows in as flows out

lines.sub: The water has not stopped. It keeps flowing.
lines.tts: The water has not stopped. It keeps flowing.

lines.sub: But as much comes in as goes out, so the amount stays the same.
lines.tts: But as much comes in as goes out, so the amount stays the same.

lines.sub: So at balance, the water in each node's cup equals the water flowing into it.
lines.tts: So at balance, the water in each node's cup equals the water flowing into it.

lines.sub: B gets 2/3 of A's water, and C gets 1/3 of A's water.
lines.tts: B gets two thirds of the water of node A, and C gets one third of it.

lines.sub: D gets all of B's and C's water.
lines.tts: D gets all of B's and C's water.

lines.sub: Nobody points to node A, so A's share is 0.
lines.tts: Nobody points to node A, so its share is zero.

lines.sub: Written in one line, it looks like this.
lines.tts: Written in one line, it looks like this.

lines.sub: Seen from one node, my share is the sum of the shares passed to me by the nodes that point to me.
lines.tts: Seen from one node, my share is the sum of the shares passed to me by the nodes that point to me.

lines.sub: The u → v under the Σ means we add only the nodes u that point to v.
lines.tts: The u, arrow, v under the sigma means we add only the nodes u that point to v.

lines.sub: Each one passes on its share, times the chance of taking the arrow to v.
lines.tts: Each one passes on its share, times the chance of taking the arrow to v.

lines.sub: This is called the balance equation.
lines.tts: This is called the balance equation.

lines.sub: But if we solve this equation all the way through, something odd happens.
lines.tts: But if we solve this equation all the way through, something odd happens.

lines.sub: A's share is 0, so B is 0 × 2/3, which is 0, and C is 0 too.
lines.tts: The share of node A is zero, so B is zero times two thirds, which is zero, and C is zero too.

lines.sub: Then D is 0 + 0, which is 0.
lines.tts: Then D is zero plus zero, which is zero.

lines.sub: On the left, every cup now reads 0.
lines.tts: On the left, every cup now reads zero.

lines.sub: The only solution of the balance equation is “all zero”.
lines.tts: The only solution of the balance equation is all zero.

lines.sub: It means all the water leaks out at D.
lines.tts: It means all the water leaks out at D.

lines.sub: We fix this problem a little later in this chapter.
lines.tts: We fix this problem a little later in this chapter.
